hardinessNote: Hardy in all of the UK and northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C.
visual: Russet-brown medlars ripen in autumn · white spring blossom · golden autumn leaves
water: Water well while establishing; established trees mainly need water during prolonged dry spells.
prune: Remove dead, damaged or crossing growth; otherwise prune lightly in the dormant season.
toxicity: Fruit flesh is edible after bletting; seeds contain toxic hydrocyanic acid and should not be eaten. Crushed or swallowed seeds may cause poisoning in people or pets.
compliance: UK plant passport required for professional movement of plants for planting.
cvs: 'Royal' – compact, good cropping · 'Westerveld' – larger fruit, reliable crops · 'Dutch' – spreading, larger-fruited
resilience: Generally robust; may get aphids or caterpillars and can be affected by quince leaf blight, brown rot, powdery mildew or honey fungus.
uses: Edible fruit · preserves and jelly · wildlife gardens · cottage gardens · specimen tree
foliage: deciduous; large leathery green leaves developing yellow-brown autumn colour
pollination: self-fertile; no pollination partner required for fruit
uncertain: Mature size varies substantially with rootstock: RHS gives 4-8 m, while commercially grafted trees on quince rootstocks are often maintained around 2.5-4 m.
Published root depth and spread specific to 'Nottingham' are insufficiently reliable, so rootSize is blank.
sunMin is an inferred practical lower tolerance; RHS specifically recommends full sun for 'Nottingham'.
